Apple új, egységes szoftverdizájnja iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26 és tvOS 26 rendszereken.[1]
 Áttetsző, üvegszerű felületi anyag, amely tükrözi és megtöri a környezet vizuális elemeit.[1]
 A színe a mögötte lévő tartalomhoz igazodik, és automatikusan alkalmazkodik világos vagy sötét megjelenéshez.[1]
 Valós idejű rendereléssel reagál a mozgásra és fénycsillanásokat jelenít meg.[1]
 Gombokon, kapcsolókon, csúszkákon, menüsorokon, oldalsávokon, appikonokon, widgeteken, a Dockon és a Vezérlőközponton is megjelenik.[1]
 Az Apple 2025. június 8án mutatta be a WWDCn.[2]

Build a complete, productionready crossplatform interface design system and reference implementation that uses an original dynamic translucent material named Prismatic Surface. Do not mention, reproduce, or depend on any preexisting software product, operating system, frameworkspecific proprietary visual system, trademark, source code, assets, or brand identity.

Construct the entire project from scratch and provide every required file in full, unabridged form: repository structure, package manifests, build configuration, source code, type definitions, styling, tests, documentation, accessibility configuration, linting, formatting, continuousintegration configuration, and deployment instructions. Do not use placeholders, mock implementations, dummy data, omitted sections, pseudocode, ellipses, or incomplete snippets. The result must build, run, test, and deploy as delivered.

Create a unified visual language for responsive web, tablet, desktop, television, and wearablesized interfaces. The system must preserve platformappropriate layout density and input behavior while sharing a consistent material, motion model, typography scale, colortoken model, icon treatment, navigation model, and component behavior across every target form factor.

Implement Prismatic Surface as a dynamic translucent interface material with all of the following characteristics:

 It must visually resemble physically plausible glass without copying any named thirdparty design language.
 It must transmit the visual influence of content behind it through configurable transparency, backdrop blur, saturation adjustment, tinting, contrast correction, and edge treatment.
 It must simulate reflected and refracted surrounding color through layered gradients, directional light, clipping, blur, and compositing.
 It must adapt its tint, luminance, opacity, border contrast, shadow, and text/icon foreground colors based on the estimated brightness and dominant color characteristics of the content behind it.
 It must support both light and dark themes and smoothly transition between themes without flashing, unreadable intermediate states, or unstable contrast.
 It must support realtime movement response through pointer position, device orientation where permission is available, scroll position, focus state, active state, hover state, and component transition state.
 It must render controlled specular highlights that move across the material surface according to the active input signal, remain visually subtle, and never reduce the readability of labels or controls.
 It must have a deterministic static fallback when realtime rendering, backdrop filtering, motion sensors, or highperformance graphics features are unavailable.
 It must respect user preferences for reduced motion, reduced transparency, increased contrast, forced colors, colorscheme preference, and batterysaving or lowperformance environments.

Use a layered rendering architecture. Define a backgroundcontent layer, an adaptive backdropsampling layer, a refractionandblur layer, a tintandcolorcorrection layer, a specularhighlight layer, a borderandinnerglow layer, a foregroundcontent layer, and an accessibility fallback layer. Ensure that each layer is independently configurable through design tokens and that the final compositing order is documented and tested.

Implement the material with progressive enhancement. Use standardsbased CSS custom properties, backdrop-filter, filter, color-mix, gradients, masks where supported, and GPUfriendly transforms. Add feature detection for unsupported browser capabilities. Provide a robust opaque or semiopaque fallback that preserves hierarchy, interaction affordances, and text contrast without relying on backdrop blur, transparency, motion effects, or experimental APIs.

Create a complete token system with semantic and componentlevel tokens. Include tokens for light and dark modes; surface opacity; blur strength; saturation; luminance lift; adaptive tint; border alpha; inner highlight alpha; outer shadow; corner radius; elevation; focus ring; content foreground colors; disabled states; hover states; pressed states; selected states; destructive actions; success states; warning states; and informational states. Include tokens for compact, regular, and spacious density modes. Define all tokens in a machinereadable source format and generate typed runtime exports and CSS variables from that source.

Build all major components using Prismatic Surface where appropriate:

 Buttons: primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive, icononly, splitbutton, loading, disabled, and toggle variants.
 Form controls: text inputs, password inputs, search inputs, text areas, selects, comboboxes, checkboxes, radios, switches, sliders, segmented controls, date/time inputs, file uploads, validation states, and error messages.
 Navigation: top bar, bottom bar, sidebar, tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, command palette, contextual menus, dropdown menus, overflow menus, and keyboard navigation.
 Containers: cards, panels, sheets, drawers, dialogs, popovers, tooltips, toasts, banners, accordions, disclosure groups, and inspector panels.
 Data presentation: tables, sortable columns, responsive table layouts, lists, tree views, badges, avatars, empty states, progress indicators, charts with accessible text equivalents, media controls, and status indicators.
 Applicationshell elements: home/dashboard grid, lockscreenstyle notification view, controlcenterstyle quick settings surface, desktop dock, launcher grid, window chrome, toolbar, and command area.
 Widget system: small, medium, and large responsive widgets that can present live status, media, calendar, weatherlike data structures, controls, and summary content without relying on proprietary service APIs.

Use the dynamic material selectively. Apply it to highlevel navigation chrome, floating controls, toolbars, panels, sheets, dialogs, sidebars, tabs, media controls, widgets, quick settings, docklike navigation, and relevant interactive elements. Avoid excessive layering: prevent nested translucent surfaces from producing muddy contrast or excessive GPU compositing. Define strict compositing budgets and enforce them through tests or runtime warnings.

Implement responsive behavior for at least five layout ranges: wearable, phone, tablet, desktop, and television. For each range, define breakpoints, typography, touchtarget requirements, keyboard behavior, focus behavior, content density, navigation transformations, panel behavior, modal behavior, and safearea handling. Support mouse, keyboard, touch, stylus, gamepadstyle directional input where available, and assistive technologies.

Implement a performance architecture that targets smooth interaction on modern hardware and graceful degradation on constrained hardware. Avoid continuous JavaScript animation loops when CSS or compositordriven animations can be used. Throttle or pause motion calculations when the document is hidden, when reduced motion is enabled, when the user is not interacting, or when performance heuristics indicate repeated dropped frames. Use requestAnimationFrame only for active visual updates that cannot be represented declaratively. Clean up all event listeners, observers, animation frames, and sensor subscriptions.

Implement adaptive backdrop analysis without collecting or transmitting user data. The system may analyze local rendered colors or explicitly supplied background metadata to choose readable surface and foreground tokens, but it must not capture screenshots, upload pixels, fingerprint devices, or make network requests for visual analysis. Provide an API that allows application code to supply background luminance and dominantcolor hints when automatic estimation is not possible.

Meet accessibility requirements throughout the implementation:

 Ensure all text and essential icons meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements in every supported theme and fallback mode.
 Ensure controls retain visible boundaries and understandable states when transparency is reduced or disabled.
 Support keyboardonly navigation, visible focus indicators, logical focus order, focus trapping in modal components, Escape handling where applicable, and restoration of focus after dialogs close.
 Use semantic HTML first, ARIA only where needed, and correct ARIA roles, states, labels, live regions, and descriptions.
 Respect prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-reduced-transparency where supported, prefers-contrast, forced-colors, and system darkmode settings.
 Ensure motion effects do not convey essential information alone.
 Provide screenreader text and nonvisual alternatives for charts, indicators, icons, and custom controls.
 Test every component with automated accessibility checks and document manual keyboard and screenreader verification procedures.

Create a demonstrator application that uses the complete component library rather than isolated component samples. Include a dashboard, navigation shell, media view, settings view, profile view, notification view, command palette, modal workflows, data table workflow, form validation workflow, theme controls, contrast controls, reducedtransparency controls, and reducedmotion controls. Populate the demonstrator only with internally defined, meaningful application content and deterministic local data. Do not depend on remote APIs, external credentials, thirdparty analytics, or proprietary content.

Implement theme and preference controls that immediately update the entire interface. Include systemdefault, forcedlight, forceddark, highcontrast, reducedtransparency, and reducedmotion modes. Persist user choices locally with explicit versioned storage and a migration strategy. Provide a resettosystemdefault control. Ensure preference changes never cause inaccessible text, flashing, focus loss, layout jumps, or temporary unstyled content.

Provide full automated testing:

 Unit tests for token generation, color calculations, luminance estimation, contrast calculations, fallback selection, theme persistence, and interactionstate transitions.
 Component tests for all component variants, keyboard interactions, focus management, validation states, disabled states, error states, and responsive rendering.
 Visual regression tests for light mode, dark mode, high contrast, reduced transparency, reduced motion, and all responsive layout ranges.
 Endtoend tests for navigation, settings persistence, dialogs, command palette, tables, forms, theme transitions, and accessibility preference changes.
 Accessibility tests using an automated accessibility engine and documented manual validation scripts.
 Performance tests that measure render cost, input latency, animation frame stability, and surfacelayer counts.
 Crossbrowser tests for current stable Chromiumbased browsers, Firefox, and WebKitbased browsers.

Include complete developer documentation. Document installation, local development, build commands, test commands, architecture, rendering layers, token schema, theming, accessibility behavior, responsive strategy, performance budgets, browser support, fallback behavior, component APIs, contribution workflow, release process, and deployment process. Document every public API with type signatures and usage examples that correspond exactly to the delivered implementation.

Set explicit quality gates. The project must fail continuous integration if type checking fails, linting fails, formatting checks fail, unit tests fail, visualregression tests fail, accessibility tests reveal serious or critical violations, production builds fail, generated token outputs differ from their sources, or performance budgets are exceeded. Configure dependency locking, reproducible builds, environment validation, security auditing, and license reporting.

Do not use copied visual assets, proprietary assets, thirdparty marks, external image hotlinking, or an existing product’s interface structure. Create all visual assets, icons, illustrations, gradients, typography decisions, and example content independently within the repository. Ensure the system is a standalone original implementation whose appearance is defined by translucent adaptive surfaces, realtime visual response, strong legibility, and accessible fallback behavior.
